subject: Altamira Dedicated Offer — onramp guardrails, minimum GPU thresholds, and activation windows
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Tobias <sarah.tobias@altamira.com>
Cc: Josh Lee <josh.lee@altamira.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Altamira Dedicated Offer — onramp guardrails, minimum GPU thresholds, and activation windows

Hi Sarah / Josh,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — enjoyed the deep dive on your real-time inference runway and model mix. As promised, attached is a concise dedicated reservation proposal that maps to the usage profiles you shared (conversational + reranking + batch embedding jobs). We focused on three things you asked to see: a) minimum committed baseline to secure predictable latency, b) a practical ramp/onramp schedule to limit burn in Q1 while enabling sustained throughput, and c) burst/soft-fallback options for spikes without pushing you into a larger long-term commit.

Key options summarized (see attached PDF & sizing model for numbers broken into node pools):
- Baseline Option A (Conservative): 16 GPUs guaranteed (2 nodes x 8 GPUs). Onramp Q1 -> Q3: 16 -> 24 -> 32. Best for teams prioritizing cost control and slow feature rollout.
- Baseline Option B (Balanced): 32 GPUs guaranteed (4 nodes x 8 GPUs). Onramp: 32 -> 48 (month 4) -> 64 (month 8). Includes 10% steady-state headroom and a 48h activation window for bursts.
- Baseline Option C (Aggressive): 64 GPUs guaranteed with staged activation, intended if you plan heavy parallel embeddings + low-latency chat at scale.

Operational guardrails we recommend:
- Soft floor (min-guarantee) + burst lanes: soft floor enforces billing/availability for minimum GPUs; burst lanes let you burst up to 2x baseline for short windows (policy-controlled).
- Activation windows: we propose monthly activation checkpoints tied to traffic markers (SLO breach triggers can accelerate activation). Typical activation times: 48–72 hours to spin up model warm pools and KV cache pre-warming.
- Credit and price structure: first 30 days of onboarding we include 25% compute-credit to offset warmup burn; multi-quarter commits get stepped discounts on per-GPU token rates.

Attachments: Altamira_Dedicated_Proposal_20270506.pdf (proposal summary + contract exhibit), GPU_Sizing_Model_Altamira.xlsx (node-level simulation).

Next steps:
1) Tell me which baseline option you want to anchor (A, B, or C) and whether you prefer a 6- or 12-month ramp cadence.
2) If you want, we can schedule a 60-min ops workshop to finalize activation windows and KV-cache warm strategies next week.

Happy to iterate.

— Irene 
Irene Choi
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

From: Sarah Tobias <sarah.tobias@altamira.com>

Cc: Josh Lee <josh.lee@altamira.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Altamira Dedicated Offer — onramp guardrails, minimum GPU thresholds, and activation windows

Thanks, Irene — this is very helpful and practical. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our infra and finance teams before we pick a baseline:

1) Minimum guaranteed baseline: for Option B (32 GPUs), is the 32 GPUs enforced as a hard reserve for the entire billing period or can we convert a portion into burst-only capacity after month 6?
2) Warmup burn: can you quantify the typical token and GPU-hour burn during the 48–72h activation window? Our CFO wants a conservative burn estimate to sit next to the onboarding credits.
3) SLA and fallback: if our primary region has an incident, what fallback latency guarantees exist if you route to secondary region capacity—do we get preserved KV cache affinity?

Also, two asks on timing: we prefer a 6-month ramp but need a legal/ procurement review first. Can you add a short clause that describes the decommit window after month 3 (e.g., 30-day decommit notice) for financial review?

If you can answer those points I can push this to procurement.

— Sarah
VP, Platform Engineering
Altamira Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Altamira Dedicated Offer — need numbers for warmup burn + legal-friendly decommit clause

Irene / team — see answers below (keeping language customer-friendly but preserving our guardrails):

Warmup burn (conservative):
- For a 32-GPU baseline (4 x 8-GPU nodes) with mixed workloads (chat + embeddings) expect ~7–10 GPU-hours per node during a full 48h warmup if we pre-populate KV caches and run representative synthetic traffic. That maps to ~28–40 GPU-hours total (32 GPUs * ~1.0–1.25 avg HVAC-normalized-hours) but to be conservative we recommend quoting 50 GPU-hours to CFO. Token burn estimate: roughly 75–120M tokens of mixed priority traffic across the 48h window (higher if you pre-warm long-context retrieval flows).

Decommit clause (suggested customer-friendly wording):
- "Decommit window: After month 3 of the term, Customer may reduce the committed GPU baseline by up to 25% with 30 days' written notice. Reductions beyond 25% require mutual agreement and may be subject to early-termination fees described in Exhibit B. Billing for the reduced baseline will take effect at the start of the next billing cycle following the 30-day notice."

SLA/fallback notes:
- We preserve KV cache affinity only within the same region. If we failover to secondary region during an incident, we provide equivalent compute capacity but recommend a short cold-cache period (estimated 2–6 minutes per model depending on context length) while KV affinity and prefix caches rebuild. We include a 10% credit if failover causes >3% p95 latency regressions for more than 30 consecutive minutes.

Pricing tweak (optional):
- Offer a one-time "warmup credit" equal to 30 GPU-hours if they commit to a 12-month baseline; otherwise we hold to the onboarding 25% compute-credit in the proposal.

If you want, I can drop this language into the proposal PDF and a short exhibit for legal.

— Marissa
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Altamira Dedicated Offer — onramp guardrails, minimum GPU thresholds, and activation windows

Sarah — quick update and answers inline: we appreciate the procurement runway.

1) Baseline convertibility: For Option B the 32 GPUs are billed as a hard reserve while committed; however the "decommit window" above lets you reduce baseline by up to 25% after month 3 with 30 days' notice. We can also include an addendum to convert up to 8 GPUs to burst-only capacity after month 6 (subject to availability windows) — that would be a documented operational change in Exhibit C.

2) Warmup burn: Marissa recommends we show a conservative number of 50 GPU-hours and 100M tokens for the 48h activation window (we'll call out range in the exhibit: 28–50 GPU-hours; 75–120M tokens). We'll add the 30 GPU-hour warmup credit if you consider a 12-month anchor.

3) SLA/fallback: we preserve KV affinity intra-region; failover to secondary region will result in cold-cache behavior (2–6 minutes dependent on model/context). We will include a 10% service credit trigger tied to sustained p95 latency regressions (>30 mins) during failover.

Next steps: 1) If that works, I'll update the attached proposal exhibit (short legal-friendly paragraph) and re-send with DocuSign link so procurement/legal can review. 2) Ops workshop: propose Tue 11 May 09:00 PT — I'll invite Karthik and Ben for the technical session.

If you'd like me to draft the two-line clause for procurement now, I can paste it into the DocuSign routing envelope so legal sees the exact language.

Cheers,
Irene
